requirements.requirement: GRUB/grubby configuration on node1 persistently includes audit=1 in kernel boot parameters (bootloader config for all kernel entries)
requirements.summary: Executor updated GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX in /etc/default/grub, applied audit=1 to all grubby kernel entries (default and rescue), regenerated /boot/grub2/grub.cfg, and directly verified both linux16 lines in grub.cfg contain audit=1 (count=2). This was re-verified after the reboot, confirming the on-disk bootloader config is intact for future boots.

requirements.requirement: The audit=1 setting survives a reboot, i.e. node1 actually boots with audit=1 active after a restart
requirements.summary: A pre-restart baseline was captured (boot_id 809708f3..., live cmdline lacked audit=1), a reboot was triggered and acknowledged, the node was polled through two timeouts until it came back with a new boot_id (69dbbb3c...) proving an actual restart occurred, and post-reboot /proc/cmdline, dmesg, and auditctl -s all confirm audit=1 is active in the newly booted kernel. This directly demonstrates the healthy baseline, disruption, and recovered/verified state required for a restart-related outcome.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — persistent audit=1 bootloader configuration and confirmed survival of that setting across an actual reboot — are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: grub.cfg and grubby entries were verified to contain audit=1 both before and after a real reboot (boot_id changed from 809708f3... to 69dbbb3c...), and the post-reboot running kernel's /proc/cmdline, auditctl -s, and dmesg all confirm audit=1 is active. Hygiene is good; only minor, low-risk residue (config backups, a reboot log) remains, which is normal and expected for this kind of bootloader change.
limitations: Only a single reboot cycle was observed, so long-term persistence across multiple future reboots is inferred from the durable on-disk grub.cfg/grubby state rather than directly re-tested.

Package-health checks timed out on both before_prepare and after_executor snapshots, so no independent confirmation of package manager consistency is available (not relevant to this task's contract, but noted per protocol).

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor's mutations were all directly tied to the task: backing up /etc/default/grub and /boot/grub2/grub.cfg before editing (cmd-ec8cc14f6ea348ed), editing GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX, applying grubby --update-kernel=ALL, regenerating grub.cfg, and triggering a reboot to verify persistence (cmd-64cc717b41f543d6). Minor residue was left behind and not cleaned up: the timestamped backup files (/etc/default/grub.bak.*, /boot/grub2/grub.cfg.bak.*) created during cmd-ec8cc14f6ea348ed, and /tmp/reboot.log created by the reboot trigger command (visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot). These are bounded, low-risk, non-destructive artifacts consistent with standard change-management practice (keeping a config backup) rather than unwanted mutations, so they only modestly reduce the hygiene score. No failed services, unsafe exposure, or damaged package state were introduced; the after_executor snapshot shows failed-services empty and listening-sockets unchanged in composition (only PIDs differ, expected after reboot).
